Regarding the raw material mentioned in 4.2, whether or not processing or production, such as slaughtering, dressing, evisceration, dividing and chopping, was carried out in a sanitary manner based on equal or better criteria than those of your country?

Abattoirs shall have stockyard facilities, ante-mortem inspection facilities, processing rooms, cooling installations, inspection rooms, disinfection facilities, segregation facilities and waste treatment facilities.

Stockyard facilities shall be provided with partitions for each head of cattle or horse over one year of age and for appropriate numbers of other livestock, which are able to pen or hold animals and shall have floors constructed of impermeable materials (meaning stone, concrete, and other materials impermeable to blood and wastewater, the same applies hereinafter) which are provided with appropriate slopes and drainage gutters.
Ante-mortem inspection facilities shall meet the following conditions.
Floors shall be constructed of impermeable materials.
Ante-mortem inspection facilities shall be equipped with apparatus necessary for cleaning or disinfecting the fingers of, and instruments used by inspectors.
Processing rooms shall meet the following conditions.

Processing rooms shall be partitioned into slaughter rooms, diseased animal slaughter rooms, viscera handling rooms, and hide handling rooms; and each room shall be provided with entrances and exits leading directly outside the processing rooms.
Floors shall be constructed of impermeable materials and shall be provided with appropriate slopes and drainage gutters.
Inside walls, except when constructed of impermeable materials, shall be covered with impermeable materials from the floor up to at least 1.2 meters.
Processing rooms shall be provided with windows allowing sufficient ventilation and natural lighting.
Processing rooms shall be equipped with viscera examination tables, viscera processing tables, viscera transportation equipment, meat hangers, and scales.
Processing rooms shall be equipped with apparatus necessary for cleaning or disinfecting the fingers of, and instruments used by, persons who slaughter or dress animals and the inspectors.

Processing rooms shall be equipped with hot water supplying installations allowing a sufficient supply of hot water needed for cleaning or disinfecting. Processing rooms shall be equipped with water supplying installations allowing a sufficient supply of drinkable water.
Inspection rooms shall be equipped with inspection tables and other equipment needed for inspections and shall be provided with waterline connections.

Disinfection facilities shall be provided with the facilities necessary for disinfection of those parts of animals which are considered to be a potential cause of disease transmission and shall have floors constructed of impermeable materials.
Segregation facilities shall be provided with facilities able to disinfect the water and wastewater of segregated livestock and shall have floors constructed of impermeable materials.
Waste treatment facilities shall meet the following conditions.

Waste treatment facilities shall have waste tanks and treatment facilities for blood and wastewater. Provided, However, That abattoirs flushing blood and waste-water directly into sewage systems with terminal treatment plants may omit treatment facilities for blood and wastewater.
Waste tanks shall be at an appropriate distance from processing rooms and trading rooms and shall be constructed of impermeable materials and be provided with appropriate covers.
Treatment facilities for blood and wastewater shall be at an appropriate distance from processing rooms and trading rooms and shall have blood and wastewater cleaning apparatus.
General provision

By giving proper cleaning, maintain the abattoir in no trouble from the viewpoint of sanitation. The abattoir shall be arranged and put in order, and unnecessary things shall be kept out of the abattoir.
In cases where there are ruptures or failures in floors, inner walls, ceilings, windows or doors, they shall be repaired or mended without delay.
The abattoir shall be fully ventilated to remove foul odor and excessive humidity.
Necessary illuminance shall be secured by means of natural illumination or lighting equipment. Perform exterminating operation at regular intervals to control of rats and insects.
In cases where ventilation equipment is installed, provide proper maintenance of said equipment.
Sanitation control of water supply installation shall be done in accordance with the following.
Any water supply shall use potable water.

In cases where disinfecting equipment or water purifying equipment is used, certify every day that the said equipment is working normally. In these cases, keep records including the date of the confirmation, the result of the confirmation, the person who confirmed and other necessary.
In cases where water storage tanks are used, inspect and clean them periodically.

In cases where refrigerating installations are used, provide proper maintenance of said installations so that they can keep the temperature of dressed carcasses or viscera for human consumption at 10 degrees centigrade or lower. In these cases, measure the temperature inside the refrigerating installations once before the beginning of daily hours of operation and once or more during the hours, and keep a record of necessary matters including the day and time of the measurement, the temperature and the person who did the measurement.
Dressed carcasses reserved by the test shall be separated from other dressed carcasses.
Sanitation control of stockyard facilities and ante-mortem inspection facilities shall be performed in accordance with the following.
Properly dispose of feces, etc., of livestock and wash the area.
Livestock with large amounts of feces, etc., on it shall be washed.
A chamber in which hide of livestock is treated shall be kept clean.
Drainage ditches shall be cleaned so that solid matter will not flow away and waste water will be properly drained out, and shall be immediately repaired when damaged.
Cleaning and disinfecting inside an abattoir shall be performed in accordance with the following.
In order to wash parts with blood or fat, etc., attached, use hot water.
Washing after the end of work shall be done using detergents.
Washing other than mentioned in a. and b. shall be done using sufficient amounts of water, hot water or detergents.
Disinfection shall be performed using hot water of a temperature of 83 degrees centigrade or higher, or disinfectants.
Sanitary control of machinery and equipment shall be performed in accordance with the following.
Machinery and equipment shall be washed or disinfected after the end of work.
Machinery and equipment, and disassembled parts of them shall be kept sanitarily each in a fixed place.

Machinery and equipment shall be checked at regular intervals and when there are failures or ruptures, repair or fix them immediately and maintain them so that they can be used properly all the time. Measuring instruments including thermometers, manometers and flow meters shall be checked at regular intervals as to their accuracy and when there are failures or abnormalities, make repairs without delay.
Sanitary control of non-edible parts shall be performed in accordance with the following.

Non-edible parts and discarded matter shall be put into exclusive containers with the labels for the discarded matter, carried away from the processing room, and shall be treated in ways that will prevent it from causing sanitary trouble.
Containers mentioned in above shall be washed and disinfected at a fixed place after completion of the work.
Control of rats, insects and the like shall be performed in accordance with the following.
Windows and doorways without controlling equipment against rats and insects shall not be left open.
Controlling equipment against rats and insects including rat screens and insect screens shall be checked as to its function and shall be repaired if necessary.

In order to prevent invasion of insects by means of containers carried into processing rooms, those containers shall be checked at the time of the receipt, and containers which have become useless shall be removed from the processing rooms and shall be disposed of in a manner that will prevent them from causing sanitary trouble, such as by incineration in an incinerator.
Lavatories shall be kept clean and disinfected at regular intervals.
Instruments for cleaning shall be kept in a designated place.
Handling of detergents, disinfectants and agents including rodenticides and insecticides shall be performed in accordance with the following.
They shall be stored in designated places other than processing rooms and places for keeping dressed carcasses.
Use agents with proper methods.
Prevent agents from contaminating carcasses, dressed carcasses and viscera for human consumption.

In cases where containers of detergents, disinfectants, etc., have been newly unsealed, preserve the record of necessary matters including the date of unsealing, the name of the agent unsealed, and the name of the person who unsealed the agent, for a year after the unsealing of the agent.

In cases where rodenticides and insecticides have been used, preserve the record of necessary matters including the date of the use, the name and used quantity of the agent used, and the name of the person who used the agent, for a year after the date of the use.
Provide control in accordance with the following to ensure that measures prescribed in the preceding items in this paragraph shall be taken properly.
Draw up a document necessary in order to carry out the measures properly and systematically.
Station a sanitation manager in order to good sanitary control of the abattoir and to check that measures have been properly carried out pursuant to the document mentioned.
Fabrication

In processing rooms, properly treat blood and contents of the digestive tracts of livestock and wash the processing room. In this case, prevent the contamination of carcasses, dressed carcasses and viscera for human consumption by the spread of washing water.

Machinery and instruments that directly contact carcasses, such as knives and saws (including saws for Halving (the process of cutting the dressed carcass right and left along the vertebral column) ) shall be washed and disinfected using hot water of a temperature of 83 degrees centigrade or higher, each time an animal has been processed (in cases where they are contaminated by the contents of the digestive tracts, on all such occasions).
When fingers have been contaminated by the blood, hide, the contents of the digestive tracts etc., wash the fingers each time using detergents.
Prevent contamination of living animal or other carcasses by the blood released by the bleeding.

Extraction of viscera shall be performed to prevent the carcass from being contaminated by the contents of the digestive tract. With regard to cattle, sheep and goats, ligate or block the esophagus in a place near the rumen in order to prevent the contents of digestive tracts from leaking out after the bleeding. When processing parts surrounding the anus of cattle, sheep and goats, ligate the rectum near the anus to prevent the contents of the digestive tracts from leaking out, and at the same time prevent the contamination of the carcass by the anal part.
When washing skinned heads, prevent the scattered washing water from contaminating other carcasses.
Skinning of carcasses; In the case where the skinned part has been contaminated by outer skin, the contents of the digestive tract, cut off entirely the contaminated part.
In cases where the skinned part has been contaminated by hide, the contents of the digestive tracts etc., cut off the contaminated part entirely.
Excision of breasts shall be performed in order to prevent the contents of the breasts from leaking out.
Extraction of viscera shall be performed in order to prevent the carcass from being contaminated by the contents of the digestive tracts.

Washing of dressed carcasses: Before the washing, ensure that there is no contamination by hair of livestock, contents of the digestive tract and the like, and when there is such contamination, cut off the contaminated part entirely.
Wash using a sufficient amount of water and prevent the dressed carcasses from being contaminated by the spread of washing water.
Drain the washing water thoroughly.
Treat dressed carcasses and viscera for human consumption to prevent them from contacting the floor, inner walls, boots and platform.
Refrigerate dressed carcasses or viscera for human consumption so that their temperature falls to 10 degrees centigrade or lower.
Hide shall be stored in a way preventing it from contacting dressed carcasses or viscera for human consumption.
The digestive tracts shall be treated separately in order to prevent the other viscera from being contaminated by the contents of the digestive tracts.
When treating the digestive tracts, remove the contents of the digestive tracts in order to prevent contamination by the contents, and wash said digestive tracts thoroughly.
In cases where the viscera-treating board has been contaminated by the contents of the digestive tracts, wash and disinfect the board on all such occasions.
The chief sanitation worker shall provide education regarding sanitary methods of slaughtering or dressing livestock to those who slaughter or dress livestock.

Presence of veterinarians during slaughter.
Mandatory information to be provided regarding health and medicine application status of animals for slaughter.

Poultry slaughtering plants are located in a place free of pollution. The ground around facilities shall be easy to clean, such as paved and drainage well.

Poultry slaughtering plants are divided in live poultry holding facility, poultry processing room, product storage room, packaging material storage room, examination room, dressing room, toilet and sewage treatment facilities respectively, and located in the appropriate position.
Any live poultry holding facilities shall have separate areas for storage and isolation of live poultry, respectively, both of which shall be properly.

Any poultry slaughtering facilities shall have a slaughtering and bleeding room, a scalding and defeathering room, and an evisceration room (which means a room with necessary equipment for evisceration; this definition shall also apply to the succeeding provisions hereof) separated from each other with partitions and properly located, and in addition, said facilities shall have inspection areas where the post feather removal inspection and the post-evisceration inspection are performed, respectively, separated from the other areas and properly located.

Live poultry holding facilities, shipping areas for slaughtered carcasses, eviscerated carcasses, and parts, and another shipping areas for inedible parts and carcasses, eviscerated carcasses, and parts determined rejectable as a result of any required inspection shall be separated from each other.

Any poultry slaughtering plant shall have enough space to keep the required sanitary level during the processes for holding live body, slaughtering, cutting, packaging, and straging of carcasses or meat.
Any floor of slaughtering facilities shall be made of impermeable materials, shall be free of any cracking or unevenness, and shall be properly inclined to drain well.
Any wall of slaughtering facilities shall be of smooth and easy-to-clean structure with no openings and shall be wainscoted with impermeable materials up to a height of necessary.
Boundary between the floor surface and the inner wall of the poultry processing facility shall be easily washed and cleaned.
Any wall of facilities other than for slaughtering shall be of smooth and easy-to-clean structure.

Any ceiling of slaughtering facilities shall be smooth and easy-to-clean structure and shall be constructed with appropriate materials as to prevent it being contaminated by mold, falling dust, or dew.
Any ceiling of facilities other than for slaughtering shall be smooth and easy-to-clean structure.
Any poultry slaughtering plant shall be so equipped as to ensure an intensity of illumination which allows inspectors or employees to perform their duties with no trouble.
An intensity of illumination of not less than 540 lx on a plane where any inspection is performed in an inspection area.
An intensity of illumination which allows employees to perform their duties with no trouble in an area other than such an inspection area referred to in Subparagraph (1) above.
An intensity of illumination which allows employees to see any live poultry, carcasses, eviscerated carcasses, or viscus in its original color.

Any ante-mortem inspection shall be performed by visually examining the conditions of live poultry before slaughtering and, if as a result of the visual examination, any one of the live poultry is suspected to suffer from one or more of the diseases or unusual conditions, by further examining all the live poultry one by one for judgment.

Any post feather-removal inspection shall be performed by visually and tactually examining all the defeathered (or feather-removed) carcasses of poultry one by one for surface conditions and, if as a result of the visual and tactual examinations, any one of the carcasses of poultry is suspected to suffer from one or more of the diseases or unusual conditions by further examining the suspected carcass of poultry for judgment.

Any post-evisceration inspection shall be performed by visually and tactually examining all the eviscerated carcasses of poultry one by one for inner surface conditions and all the viscera related to those carcasses for visceral conditions and, if as a result of the visual and tactual examinations, any of the eviscerated carcasses of poultry or the viscera is suspected to suffer from one or more of the diseases or unusual conditions by further examining the suspected viscera or eviscerated carcass of poultry for judgment.
Processing rooms shall be provided with instruments allowing sufficient ventilation.
Any poultry slaughtering plant shall be provided with the following facilities such as for water supply and hot water supply.
Water supply facilities which can supply an adequate amount of water from public supply or private sources or other drinkable water.
Hot water supply facilities which can supply an adequate amount of hot water at 60 degrees centigrade or higher.

Any drainage facilities shall have a smooth internal surface properly inclined to drain well and have drainage ditches connected to sewage treatment facilities or to a public sewage. Each of said drainage ditches shall include a trap and other means to prevent a backward flow of sewage or smell and any invasion of rodents.
That the storage facility of cleaning equipment and disinfecting equipment conforming to the purpose is located in the appropriate position.
Provide with an appropriate number of hand washing equipment for employees and inspectors.
Any live poultry holding area shall be provided with facilities for washing and disinfecting live poultry transportation containers.
Any poultry slaughtering facilities shall have facilities to store containers for inedible parts.
Any poultry slaughtering facilities shall be separated from areas in no direct connection with poultry slaughtering and the entrance doors shall be capable of closing tightly.
Provide with an appropriate number of hand washing equipment in proportion to the number of employees and inspectors.
Provide with facilities for washing and disinfecting machinery and instruments.
Prevent contamination of live animal or other carcasses by the blood released by the bleeding.
Bleeding
The bleeding area shall have the operative instruments and the facility for washing and disinfecting the instruments.
Bleeding shall be done sufficiently.
Prevent contamination of poultry carcasses and living body from blood.
Blood is shall be collected and carried out appropriately with container made ​​of impermeable materials.

Any scalding and defeathering room shall be provided with a scalding machine, a feather picking machine, and a machine for cleaning carcasses of poultry each of which has an adequate capacity in proportion to the number of poultry to be handled, and facilities for washing and disinfecting those machines.
Scalding
Carcasses is scalded promptly after bleeding.
Scalding shall be done using sufficient amounts of water and hot water.
In scalding, contaminants shall be removed from carcasses as much as possible.
Any evisceration room shall be provided with the following.

One or more overhead conveyers, belt conveyers, or vats which allow employees to make sure that an eviscerated carcass and viscera are identified with original carcass and which have a structure to prevent any contamination of other carcasses and viscera.

Equipment and utensils used for cutting off cloacae, abdominal operations, evisceration, washing the inside and outside of eviscerated carcasses, and cooling eviscerated carcasses, and facilities for washing and disinfecting them.
Facilities for washing and disinfecting overhead conveyers, belt conveyers, vats, tables, chipping boards, and other equipment and utensils used for poultry slaughtering.
An adequate number of hand washing equipment in proportion to the number of employees.
Prevent the carcass from being contaminated by other carcass mutually.
Any window, ventilating opening, or other opening connected to the outside shall have an appropriate means to prevent any invasion of insects.

Non-edible parts and discarded matter shall be put into exclusive containers with the label for the discarded matter carried away from the processing room, and shall be treated in ways that will prevent it from causing sanitary trouble.

Any evisceration room shall be provided one or more overhead conveyers, belt conveyers, or vats which allow employees to make sure that an eviscerated carcass and viscera are identified with original carcass.
Inspection area
Any inspection area shall be provided with inspection tables or racks used only for performing the inspection.
Provide with hand washing equipment used by inspectors only.

Machinery and instruments that directly contact carcasses, such as knives, saws shall be washed and disinfected using hot water of a temperature of 83 degrees centigrade or higher each time an animal has been processed.
Any inspection room shall be capable of being locked and have inspection tables and hand washing equipment.
Storage(refrigerator, freezer)
Any product storage room shall be provided with facilities for refrigerating and freezing. Cooling installations shall be capable of cooling meat thoroughly.
Dressed carcasses reserved by the inspection shall be stored separately from other dressed carcasses.
Equipment or utensil
Any equipment or utensil shall be easy to clean and shall be disinfection structure.
Any rigid equipment or utensil shall be placed in the position to be easy to operate, clean and disinfect.
Any live poultry transportation containers shall be made of impermeable materials and their structure shall be easy to wash and disinfect.

Any containers for slaughtered carcasses and eviscerated carcasses passing all inspections or edible parts shall be made of impermeable materials, shall be exclusive and shall be the structures to be easy to clean and wash.
Any containers for non-edible parts and discarded matter shall be made of impermeable materials, shall be with cover and shall be the structures to be easy to clean and wash.
If use over-head-conveyer, it shall be made of impermeable materials and shall be with washer disinfector for the shackles.
Any feather removal facilities shall be with a structure to prevent any scatter feathers and a feature to spray water.
Any auto-cloaca-removal, auto-abdominal retractor and auto-evisceration shall be with auto washer disinfector.

Any equipment or utensil, for example belt conveyers, vats, tables, chipping boards and other equipment for poultry slaughtering, that are in direct contact with any live poultry, eviscerated carcasses or parts, shall be made of impermeable materials and shall be easy to wash and disinfect.
Others
Any locker room shall have enough space in proportion to the number of employees and have storage facilities used only for their boots, aprons, and working clothes.

Any lavatory shall be separated from other areas with partitions, and shall have no entrance door directly connected with any poultry slaughtering facilities or have other means to prevent said lavatory from affecting any poultry slaughtering facilities.
Any lavatory shall be provided with hand washing equipment.
Any window, ventilating opening, or other opening connected to the outside shall have an appropriate means to prevent any invasion of insects.
Waste treatment facilities shall have blood and wastewater cleaning apparatus.

Both the inside and the outside of any eviscerated carcass which passes the post-evisceration inspection or which is verified compliant with the Standards for inner surface conditions shall be thoroughly washed with a proper amount of water.

Any viscera which pass the post-evisceration inspection or which are verified compliant with the Standards for visceral conditions shall be divided into edible and inedible parts, and the edible parts shall be thoroughly washed.
Abdominal incision for evisceration inspection shall be done as far as exam and confirmation become practicable.
Any organs shall be withdrawn to inspect and verify.
Any eviscerated carcasses and their parts shall be operated with any means to prevent contamination of gut contents.
Any washed carcass, eviscerated carcass, or parts shall be promptly cooled down at 10 degrees centigrade or lower.
Any carcasses, eviscerated carcasses and parts shall be refrigerated in refrigerated water made by water cooler or other means through ventilating, if refrigerating them by refrigerated water.
Any cooling bath used shall be washed and disinfected after empty it out.
Dressed carcasses reserved by the inspection shall be stored separately from other dressed carcasses.
Employee
Requiring any employee to control their own health condition and have a medical checkup as necessary.
Requiring any employee not to go to the lavatory with apron.
Requiring any employee to wear clean working clothes and caps and footgear which are used only in the work place and not to wear unnecessary accessories.

Requiring any employee to keep the hands clean and to wash and disinfect them before the employee starts work, after the employee goes to a lavatory, and after the employee touches anything that may contaminate any edible parts.

Any poultry slaughterer shall remove the employees who suffers from a superlative disease or any other disease that may be transmitted through poultry parts from a slaughtering line in the abattoir or poultry slaughtering plant.
Requiring any employee to change the clothes, to smoke, to expectorate, and to eat some food at a designated place, respectively.
Any poultry slaughterer shall keep any unauthorized person other than the employees away from the abattoir or poultry slaughtering plant without reasonable reasons.
The poultry slaughterer or the chief sanitation worker shall provide education regarding sanitary methods of slaughtering or dressing poultry to those who slaughter or dress poultry.

Whether or not poultry processing plants are obligated to manage hygiene procedures based on HACCP principles? If no, whether or not individual establishments implement hygiene management based on HACCP principles according to request from exporting countries?
Regarding the sanitary control associated with live poultry, poultry carcass, eviscerated carcass, or the parts, the following measures shall be taken.
A document describing the following items shall be prepared.

Measures to prevent the substances which may cause food sanitation hazards and the relevant hazards which may occur in the relevant processes from occurring (hereinafter referred to as “control measures”) for each process including the reception of live poultry, bleeding, scalding, defeathering, evisceration and cooling (when no relevant substance which may cause hazards can be found, the reason is to be stated).

The processes of (i) in which the implementation status of the control measures associated with the relevant process need to be checked continuously or at a fair frequency (hereinafter referred to as“critical control point”) in order to prevent food sanitation hazards associated with the products (when a critical control point is not determined, the reason is to be stated).

Criteria of the control measures for each of all of the critical control points in order to reduce to an acceptable range or eliminate the substances which may cause food sanitation hazards which may occur at the relevant critical control point.
Method to confirm (ii) (monitoring at the critical control points)

A document describing the method of the improvement measures which shall be taken when the control measures associated with the critical control points are not found to be taken properly upon the confirmation of c (ii) shall be prepared.
A document describing the method to verify that the testing method of the products is properly preventing food sanitation hazards shall be prepared.
A document describing the recording method and the method and duration of storage of the relevant records shall be prepared for the following items.
Items regarding the confirmation of (c) (ii)
Items regarding the improvement measures of (d)
Items regarding the verification of (e)

According to the documents prepared based on the provisions of (a) to (d), measures necessary for public health shall be taken in order to prevent food sanitation hazards associated with live poultry, poultry carcass, eviscerated carcass, or the parts for human consumption.
Provide control in accordance with the following to ensure that measures prescribed in the preceding items in this paragraph shall be taken properly.
Draw up a document necessary in order to carry out the hygiene measures properly .(draw up SSOP)
